clue.text: Passing fashion pursued by editor is no longer prominent

blocks.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A trend that the editor has finally caught up with has already lost its prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursued by' simply means the editor's abbreviation comes after the craze.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has dimmed or lost its colour has stopped standing out, so it is less conspicuous than before.

clue.text: Blossoming fig initially having a dark look

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the first letter of fig
lowering, said of the sky or a face, means dark and threatening

explanation.surface: A fig tree in bloom somehow looks gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowering here rhymes with flowering and means scowling or overcast, not bringing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is flowering is producing blooms, which is what blossoming means.

clue.text: Revolted after scoundrel does for flower

blocks.note: a dog is a contemptible man
to rise up is to revolt

explanation.surface: People rebelled after a villain killed off a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolted' looks like disgusted, but means rebelled; 'after' places it behind the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose common in European hedgerows, bearing pink or white blooms.

clue.text: Rename quad foolishly? I’ll be dreadfully outraged

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means doing it wrongly, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: If anyone renames the college quadrangle, someone promises to be furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A quad is a college courtyard. The definition is a self-description in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama queen is someone who reacts to everything with exaggerated emotion, so overblown outrage is the trait.

clue.text: Call Lord stupid after rebuffing intermediary

indicators.note: to rebuff is to push back, so the words before this phrase are read backwards

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them
LD is the abbreviation for Lord
dim means slow-witted

explanation.surface: Someone snubbed a go-between and then called a peer an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After rebuffing' looks like a time sequence, but it tells you the whole string of call, Lord and stupid is turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman is a go-between who stands between two parties in a deal, a synonym for intermediary.

clue.text: Full development? I may trust to ignore son misbehaving

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is removed
misbehaving means acting out of line, so the remaining letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent hopes that a grown child will stop misbehaving and become trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Maturity is the state of being fully grown, the end point of development.

clue.text: Fix entrance, allowing Court to enter

indicators.note: allowing something in means letting it inside, so one piece goes within the other
entering means going inside, which confirms the court letters sit within the doorway word

blocks.note: a door is a way in
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Repair the doorway so that court officials can come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' is a verb meaning tamper with, as in doctoring the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to falsify or rig it, just as to fix a result is to tamper with it.

clue.text: Courage yielding power and fortune

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so the courage word surrenders a letter

blocks.note: pluck is spirit and bravery
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Bravery gives way to strength and good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck and fortune both mean chance, the force that brings good or bad things by accident.

clue.text: A little approach to work taking on timeless maxim

indicators.note: timeless means without time, so the letter for time is removed

blocks.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working
a dictum is a saying

explanation.surface: A modest work ethic that adopts an eternal saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' sounds like praise for the maxim, but it tells you to drop T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount of something, as in a modicum of sense.

clue.text: Erotic writer retaining kiss and hug for former President

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so the writer's name holds other letters inside

blocks.note: Anaïs Nin was known for her erotic fiction and diaries
X for a kiss and O for a hug, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An author of erotica keeps a love letter's sign-off to a former US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th President of the United States, resigning in 1974 after Watergate.

clue.text: Wild licentious Italian family dismissing book given a lot of credit

indicators.note: dismissing something sends it away, so a letter is dropped from the family name
a lot of something is not all of it, so the final letter of the credit word goes

blocks.note: the Borgias were a Renaissance Italian family notorious for vice
B is the abbreviation for book
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A dissolute Italian dynasty, expelling a bookish member, was granted plenty of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild licentious' looks like one description, but 'Wild' alone is the definition and 'licentious' belongs to the family. Buying on tick means buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic behaviour is unrestrained and frenzied, like that at an orgy, so it is wild in the sense of uncontrolled.

clue.text: Former partner is behind fake manuscript

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means mock or sham, as in cod philosophy
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: An ex has been caught out as the forger of a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is behind' places the former partner after the word for fake. Cod meaning sham is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A codex is an ancient handwritten book, a bound manuscript rather than a scroll.

clue.text: Involved re orca row? I will step in: I fight for the planet

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so these letters are jumbled
stepping in means entering, so the single letter goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the first of the two I's in the clue, the one that will step in

explanation.surface: An activist explains joining a quarrel about killer whales to defend the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person, as if the answer were speaking about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is an environmental activist who campaigns, sometimes militantly, to protect the natural world.

clue.text: Look over small quantity of film

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
film reels are stored in cans, hence in the can

explanation.surface: Someone checks a short piece of footage.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page or scene is to run your eyes quickly over it, to examine it briefly.

clue.text: Dream character upset re TV signal

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in a fantasy is distressed about a television signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream' is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, not a dream in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Starveling the tailor is one of the rude mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: I desire to backtrack, about to abandon unbalanced state

indicators.note: backtracking is going back the way you came, so the word for desire is read backwards
about means around, so the reversed letters wrap round the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a yen is a longing
to quit is to leave or give up

explanation.surface: Someone wants to retreat, ready to give up on a lopsided situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed desire is split by the word for abandon, which goes inside it just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity is unfairness or injustice, a lack of balance between what parties receive.

clue.text: I’m back, probing three letters, covering the smallest things?

indicators.note: back signals that the contraction is read in the backward direction
something probing pushes inside, so these letters sit within the run of letters

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
A to C spans exactly three letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone returns to examine a short acronym that seems to cover tiny things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three letters' are not an abbreviation but the range A to C, written out.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic relates to atoms, the tiny particles of matter, hence the question mark on a playful definition.

clue.text: Saintly writer is supporting rights document

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the little word comes after the document

blocks.note: a charter is a document granting rights
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy author is backing a human rights declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supporting means placed underneath. 'Saintly' is not about holiness: Leslie Charteris created Simon Templar, the Saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Leslie Charteris wrote the novels about Simon Templar, known as The Saint, so he is the writer of the Saint.

clue.text: Forgetting US university money’s invested in other governments initially

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so these letters go inside
initially points to the first letters of the words it follows

blocks.note: the first letters of other and governments
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: An American university's funds are placed with foreign governments, then overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin as a word for money is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitting something is leaving it out, often by forgetting to include it.

clue.text: Most favourable target after dumping American study?

indicators.note: dumping means throwing away, so a letter is removed from the target word

blocks.note: a goal is an aim
A is the abbreviation for American
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: The best aim, apparently, is to drop research done in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a placing instruction, but it belongs to the removal of A from GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden opportunity is an excellent, highly advantageous one, so golden means very favourable.

clue.text: Left unable to accommodate feet? Prepare space to stretch out

indicators.note: unable to accommodate means having no room for, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for feet
to groom is to make ready

explanation.surface: Someone left without space for their feet urges others to make room to stretch out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'feet' standing for its abbreviation FT, removed from LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space in front of a seat in which a passenger can extend their legs.

clue.text: Married relative filling large part of the world with good stuff

indicators.note: filling something means occupying its inside, so these letters go within the continent

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
bro is short for brother
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A married relative settling in a huge continent, bringing plenty of fine things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link but the definition is 'good stuff', a playful take on food of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia is the food of the Greek gods, so by extension anything delicious and delightful.

clue.text: Promise to hem edges of teenage clothing item

indicators.note: to hem is to enclose with a border, so the promise word goes round
edges are the outermost parts, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: to swear is to vow
first and last letters of teenage

explanation.surface: A parent pledges to take up the hem of a teenager's garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hem' sounds like dressmaking, fitting the clothing surface, but it means surround. A sweater is a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted pullover, a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Ocean process taking different line before turning active

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so the letters are rearranged
turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
on means operating or active

explanation.surface: A procedure involving the sea changes course before becoming lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places the rearranged letters ahead of the reversed ones.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is a periodic warming of the eastern Pacific that disrupts weather worldwide, an oceanic phenomenon.

clue.text: Imprison a lot of sailors dodging bloodbath

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the bloodbath word leaves those letters out

blocks.note: carnage is mass slaughter
RN, the Royal Navy, is a lot of sailors, followed by A

explanation.surface: Lock up a crowd of sailors who have escaped a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy (RN) stands for a body of sailors; with 'a' it makes the run of letters lifted from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage a person or animal is to confine them behind bars, a verb synonym for imprison.

clue.text: Church in America, a friendly kind

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church; that these words also happen to contain the answer running through them is a coincidence
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A welcoming congregation found in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as placing the church inside America but is just a piece of the answer. China plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, so a china is a friend, one of a friendly sort.

clue.text: Everyone in historic city beginning to transmit good wishes

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is taken

blocks.note: all means everybody
Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt and also of Greece
the opening letter of transmit

explanation.surface: Everyone in an ancient city starts sending greetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like an instruction to put one thing inside another, but here the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: All the best is a standard farewell phrase expressing goodwill, often used to sign off letters.

clue.text: Where the dying go, we stay? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only part, so half of the final word's letters are lost

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Those on their deathbed depart while we remain; something like a riddle about mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: To go west is an idiom for dying. 'Not half' looks like British slang for 'very much', but here it trims the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To go west is an old idiom for to die, so the dying head in that direction.

clue.text: Combined Institute backed by nobody

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for Institute
none means not one person

explanation.surface: A merged institute that nobody is willing to support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' suggests reversal, but it only means the institute's letter is followed by the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things in one are merged into a single item, as with an all-in-one appliance, hence combined.

clue.text: Founder working air into it

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A metalworker in a foundry is pumping air into the mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' suggests foundry work, but here it means the person who starts something.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder establishes or starts an enterprise, and an initiator is likewise the one who sets something going.

clue.text: Space pioneer’s endeavour mostly captured in power ballad

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the effort word is dropped
something captured in another thing is held inside it

blocks.note: military power or weaponry: arms
a try is an attempt
the rest of a song, which wraps round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: An astronaut's achievement is largely celebrated in a rousing rock anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power ballad' must be split: arms is power and song is ballad, with the shortened attempt sitting between their letters. Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, commander of Apollo 11, was the first human to walk on the Moon in 1969.

clue.text: Roughly half of schoolchildren rejected limitations to school outfit

indicators.note: limits are the boundaries of something, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
something rejected is sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters of school
a rig or rig-out is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: About half the pupils refused to accept the restrictions on school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and seems to be the subject of the sentence; it is a cheerful description of girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are split roughly evenly by sex, so girls make up around half of all schoolchildren.
